fields.Participants: CEO, CFO, COO, CIO, CMO, CHRO, VP Supply Chain
fields.Trigger: Monthly calendar (first week of month for prior month results)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "FP&A prepares monthly operating review package" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "reports on their area" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-track of "tracked in initiative tracker per W1660" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: CFO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Review-theater risk**: the meeting recites numbers without decisions; mitigated by the variance-flag-driven agenda and owner-tracked action items reviewed at the next monthly meeting (steps 2, 4)
- **Data-latency risk**: a late or inaccurate package erodes executive trust in the process; mitigated by the Day-3 deadline with FP&A quality checks before CFO review (steps 1–2)
System Touchpoints: - Operating review package auto-assembly (by Day 3) — P&L actual vs. budget vs. prior year, entity and consolidated, revenue/margin bridges, KPIs (step 1)
- Variance flagging engine — > 5% vs. budget or 3-month adverse-trend flags driving the agenda (step 2)
- Action-item tracker linkage — decisions routed to owners in the initiative tracker per W1660 (step 4)
Time Estimate: ~21 hours per monthly cycle (operating-review package preparation 2 days + CFO review 2 hours + Monthly Operating Review meeting 2–3 hours + action-item distribution 30 min) ≈ 250 hours/year.

steps.activity: FP&A prepares monthly operating review package (by Day 3 of month): (a) P&L summary: actual vs. budget vs. prior year (entity-level and consolidated), (b) revenue analysis: by store cluster, by category, by channel (in-store vs. ecommerce), (c) gross margin analysis: by category, with margin bridge (volume, mix, price, cost), (d) OpEx analysis: by department with variance commentary, (e) working capital dashboard: inventory days, receivable days, payable days, cash position, (f) store operations metrics: sales/sqm, inventory turns, shrinkage, on-time replenishment, (g) supply chain metrics: DC throughput, fill rate, on-time delivery, (h) ecommerce metrics: orders, GMV, conversion rate, AOV, BOPIS pickup rate, (i) HR metrics: turnover, open positions, training completion

CFO reviews package; identifies areas requiring executive discussion: (a) significant variances (> 5% vs. budget), (b) trend concerns (3+ months of unfavorable trend), (c) strategic initiative progress, (d) risk items

Monthly Operating Review meeting (Day 5–7): (a) CFO presents financial overview, (b) each C-Suite member reports on their area: key metrics, variances, actions, (c) CEO directs specific actions and follow-ups, (d) FP&A captures action items with owners and deadlines
Action items distributed to owners; tracked in initiative tracker per W1660; progress reviewed at next monthly meeting

fields.Participants: FP&A, CEO, COO, CMO, VP Store Operations
fields.Trigger: Weekly calendar (Monday for prior week results)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count and average transaction value" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-distribute of "distributed to CEO, COO, CMO, VP Store Operations by Monday 9 AM" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Noise-over-signal risk**: weekly swings trigger over-reaction (typhoon closures, holidays read as trends); mitigated by FP&A commentary separating one-off events from trend (step 2)
- **Silent-skip risk**: a failed generation or missed distribution goes unnoticed until executives ask; mitigated by scheduled auto-generation with distribution monitoring (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Auto-generated weekly sales flash (Monday 6 AM) — chain and store-cluster revenue, daily/weekly, vs. same week last year and vs. budget (step 1)
- Commentary layer and mobile executive dashboard — events, anomalies, and promotional impact distributed by Monday 9 AM (steps 2–3)
Time Estimate: 30 min per occurrence (per-step effort 30 min) — at Weekly (52×/year) ≈ 52 occurrences/year ≈ 26 hours/year.

steps.activity: System auto-generates weekly sales flash (Monday 6 AM): (a) total chain revenue: daily and weekly, vs. same week last year, vs. budget, (b) store cluster performance: Metro Manila, Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao, (c) top 10 / bottom 10 stores by revenue variance, (d) ecommerce: orders, GMV, conversion rate, (e) category performance: top 5 growing categories, top 5 declining, (f) transaction count and average transaction value, (g) key promotions performance (if active)
FP&A adds commentary: (a) significant events affecting sales (typhoon closures, holidays, competitor promotions), (b) notable trends or anomalies, (c) promotional event results if applicable
Weekly sales flash distributed to CEO, COO, CMO, VP Store Operations by Monday 9 AM; accessible via mobile executive dashboard

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Regional Managers, Store Managers
fields.Trigger: Monthly calendar (by Day 10 for prior month)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count, safety audit score" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews scorecards for their stores" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-identify of "identify root causes for underperformance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: VP Store Operations review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-gaming risk**: stores optimize scored metrics at the expense of unscored outcomes like customer experience; mitigated by the balanced financial + operational scorecard and root-cause reviews (steps 1, 3)
- **Bottom-decay risk**: chronic underperformers linger without consequence; mitigated by bottom-10 store action plans tracked under VP Store Operations/COO oversight (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Monthly store scorecard generator — financial KPIs (revenue vs. budget, margin %, controllable expense, contribution) and operational KPIs per store (step 1)
- Regional review workflow — top/bottom identification and monthly per-store review calls with corrective actions (steps 2–3)
- Chain aggregation for COO — regional comparison and bottom-10 action plans (step 4)
Time Estimate: recurring effort 4 hours/month + 2 hours/month + ~100 hours/month (200 stores × 30 min review calls) ≈ ~1,270 hours/year.

steps.activity: System generates monthly store scorecard per store: (a) financial KPIs: revenue vs. budget, gross margin %, controllable expense vs. budget, store contribution margin, (b) operational KPIs: sales/sqm, inventory turns, shrinkage %, on-time replenishment rate, (c) customer KPIs: customer satisfaction score, NPS (if surveyed), loyalty enrollment rate, (d) people KPIs: turnover rate, training completion, attendance compliance, (e) safety KPIs: incident count, safety audit score

Regional Manager reviews scorecards for their stores (~33 stores per Regional Manager; ~6 RMs per VS-177); identifies: (a) top performing stores (recognize and share best practices), (b) underperforming stores (coach and action plan), (c) stores with concerning trends (3+ months declining metrics)

Regional Manager conducts monthly review call with each Store Manager: (a) discuss scorecard results, (b) identify root causes for underperformance, (c) agree on corrective actions, (d) share best practices from top-performing stores

VP Store Operations reviews aggregate store performance with COO monthly: (a) chain-wide average scorecard, (b) regional comparison, (c) bottom 10 stores with action plans, (d) top 10 stores for recognition

workflows.name: Category Manager Monthly Performance Review & Margin Ownership

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "FP&A generates category-level monthly P&L" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews category performance with each Category Manager" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: VP Merchandising review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion-blindness risk**: mix shifts mask per-SKU margin decay; mitigated by the cost/price/mix margin bridge decomposition (step 1)
- **Action-drift risk**: the same category shortfall is reviewed monthly without vendor or price action; mitigated by category-specific action items with owner follow-through (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Category P&L generator — revenue vs. budget by category and store cluster with gross-margin bridge (cost, price, mix) (step 1)
- Assortment analytics feed — new-SKU sell-through and discontinued-item performance into the VP Merchandising review (step 2)
- Category action tracking — margin/recovery actions per category owner (step 3)
Time Estimate: 1 day elapsed per occurrence (1 day); cadence-carried steps as authored (Ongoing) — at Monthly ≈ 12 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: FP&A generates category-level monthly P&L: (a) revenue vs. budget by category and by store cluster, (b) gross margin % and margin bridge (cost change, price change, mix change, promo impact), (c) sell-through rate, (d) inventory turns and weeks of supply, (e) markdown rate, (f) vendor margin contribution (rebates, volume discounts)

VP Merchandising reviews category performance with each Category Manager: (a) revenue and margin vs. plan, (b) assortment effectiveness (new SKU sell-through, discontinued SKU clearance progress), (c) promotional ROI (margin given up vs. incremental revenue), (d) vendor negotiation wins/losses, (e) action items for margin improvement

Category-specific action items: (a) margin below target → vendor negotiation for better cost, price increase, or mix shift, (b) revenue below target → promotional plan, assortment adjustment, (c) inventory above target → markdown acceleration, return to vendor

fields.Participants: CFO, CEO, Corporate Secretary, Board of Directors

workflows.name: Quarterly Board Performance Report & Governance Package

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "technology project status, cybersecurity posture, system performance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-compile of "compiles governance package" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "records Board minutes and resolutions" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: CFO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-distribution risk**: materials arriving days before the meeting preclude informed director review; mitigated by the 5-business-day distribution rule (step 2)
- **Resolution-execution gap**: Board approvals and directions go unactioned after the meeting; mitigated by resolution communication to responsible officers with W1660 progress tracking (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Board governance package compiler — CEO report, CFO financials, committee reports (step 1)
- Board portal distribution 5 business days pre-meeting per governance policy (step 2)
- Resolution execution and filing tracker — minutes, officer execution, W1660 tracking, quarterly financial statement filings (step 4)
Time Estimate: 3–4 hours per occurrence (per-step effort 3–4 hours); elapsed timeline 1 week + 1 day + 1 week — at Quarterly (4×/year) ≈ 4 occurrences/year ≈ 12–16 hours/year.

steps.activity: CFO prepares Board governance package: (a) CEO report: strategic initiative progress, market commentary, organizational highlights, (b) CFO report: quarterly financial results vs. budget and prior year, YTD performance, revised full-year forecast, cash and debt position, (c) COO report: store operations summary, new store pipeline and openings, supply chain performance, (d) CIO report: technology project status, cybersecurity posture, system performance, (e) CMO report: marketing campaign results, ecommerce growth, loyalty program metrics, (f) CHRO report: headcount, turnover, key hires, training, (g) Internal Audit report: audit findings, management action status, (h) Risk report: top risks, risk mitigation status, emerging risks
Corporate Secretary compiles governance package; distributes to Board members 5 business days before meeting per corporate governance policy

Board meeting: (a) CEO and C-Suite present reports, (b) Board discusses performance, asks questions, provides direction, (c) Board approves: quarterly financial statements, dividend declaration (if applicable), major capex projects, policy changes, (d) Corporate Secretary records Board minutes and resolutions

Post-meeting: (a) Board resolutions communicated to relevant officers for execution, (b) management actions tracked per W1660, (c) quarterly financial statements filed with SEC (per Philippine corporate law)

fields.Participants: CHRO, CEO, C-Suite, HR, Payroll, Finance

workflows.name: Annual Performance Assessment & Incentive Compensation Calculation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compiles annual performance data" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews and calibrates performance ratings for direct reports" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-calculate of "calculated separately from performance bonus" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: CHRO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rating-inflation risk**: calibration drift overrates performance and blows the bonus budget; mitigated by tiered calibration and CEO/CHRO approval within the approved incentive budget (steps 2, 4)
- **Calculation-error risk**: manual bonus mathematics across 6,762 employees; mitigated by system-calculated payouts with HR/Payroll verification before release (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Performance data compilation — individual KPI achievement and behavioral competency assessment (step 1)
- Calibration workflow — C-Suite, Regional Manager, and distribution-level rating calibration (step 2)
- Incentive calculation engine — store bonus pools (base × multiplier × store achievement), plan funding gates, and approval workflow (steps 3–4)
Time Estimate: 6 weeks elapsed per occurrence (2 weeks + 1 week + 1 week + 1 week + 1 week) — at Annual ≈ 1 occurrence/year.

steps.activity: HR compiles annual performance data: (a) individual KPI achievement vs. targets (for roles with quantifiable KPIs), (b) behavioral competency assessment (for all roles), (c) store scorecard results (for Store Managers), (d) category P&L results (for Category Managers), (e) department operating plan achievement (for department heads)

Performance calibration: (a) C-Suite reviews and calibrates performance ratings for direct reports, (b) Regional Managers calibrate Store Manager ratings, (c) distribution guidelines: top performer (15%), strong performer (35%), solid performer (35%), development needed (12%), unsatisfactory (3%)

Incentive compensation calculation: (a) **Store Managers**: bonus = base salary × performance multiplier × store achievement %; funded from store-level P&L bonus pool, (b) **Category Managers**: bonus = base salary × category margin achievement %, (c) **HQ staff**: bonus = base salary × corporate achievement multiplier (based on consolidated EBITDA vs. target), (d) **Sales Associates**: monthly commission based on individual sales performance (tracked via POS ID), (e) **13th month pay**: mandatory per PD 851; calculated separately from performance bonus
CEO approves incentive compensation for C-Suite and department heads; CHRO approves for all other employees within approved budget
Payroll processes incentive payments; separate from regular payroll per PH tax rules; BIR withholding tax calculated on bonus income

fields.Frequency: Annual review; ad-hoc additions as strategy evolves
fields.Trigger: Annual strategic planning cycle (W1645) or new KPI introduction
fields.Volume: ~100–150 KPIs across all levels (corporate → department → store → individual)

workflows.name: KPI Definition, Target Setting & Cascading Framework

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count, ecommerce penetration, employee engagement — CEO and Board level" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-proliferation risk**: KPIs accrete without retirement, diluting focus; mitigated by governance requiring definition, owner, and reporting level per KPI with annual review (step 3)
- **Local-optimization risk**: cascaded targets invite gaming against enterprise goals; mitigated by alignment review of Tier 2/3 targets against the Tier 1 corporate set (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - KPI dictionary — ~100–150 KPIs with definition, formula, data source, frequency, target, owner, and reporting level (step 3)
- Target cascading model — Tier 1 corporate → Tier 2 department → Tier 3 store/individual decomposition (step 2)
Time Estimate: Annual target setting 2 weeks ≈ 80 hours/year cascading ~100–150 KPIs across corporate/department/store/individual tiers; quarterly KPI governance review 2 hours ≈ 8 hours/year; KPI hierarchy maintenance ongoing within FP&A.

steps.activity: FP&A maintains KPI hierarchy: (a) **Tier 1 (Corporate)**: Revenue, EBITDA margin, net income, cash flow, ROIC, store count, ecommerce penetration, employee engagement — CEO and Board level, (b) **Tier 2 (Functional)**: Category margin, DC fill rate, store sales/sqm, customer NPS, inventory turns, system uptime, turnover rate — C-Suite level, (c) **Tier 3 (Operational)**: POS transaction speed, GR processing time, AP days payable outstanding, AR days sales outstanding, website conversion rate, DC picks per hour — Manager level, (d) **Tier 4 (Individual)**: Sales per associate, picking accuracy, invoice processing time, first-call resolution rate — Individual contributor level

Annual target setting: (a) Tier 1 targets set during strategic planning (W1645), (b) Tier 2 targets decomposed from Tier 1 by C-Suite, (c) Tier 3 targets set by department heads aligned to Tier 2, (d) Tier 4 targets set by managers aligned to Tier 3

KPI governance: (a) each KPI has: name, definition, calculation formula, data source, measurement frequency, target, owner, reporting level, (b) FP&A maintains KPI dictionary; no ad-hoc KPI creation without FP&A review, (c) quarterly: FP&A reviews KPI relevance; proposes additions/modifications to CFO

fields.Frequency: Ongoing tracking; monthly reporting to C-Suite
fields.Trigger: Strategic initiative approved in W1645 or emerging priority
fields.Volume: ~15–25 active cross-functional initiatives at any time

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documented in initiative tracker" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "update" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-compile of "compiles initiative status summary for CEO" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-341 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Performance Management (PA-33.2).)
- operational: CEO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Zombie-initiative risk**: stalled efforts consume budget indefinitely; mitigated by monthly CEO/C-Suite portfolio review with course-correct or kill decisions (step 4)
- **Status-greenwashing risk**: leads report green until sudden failure; mitigated by milestone-level evidence cross-checked against budget utilization (steps 2–3)
System Touchpoints: - Initiative tracker — sponsor, lead, business case, milestones, budget for ~15–25 active cross-functional initiatives (step 1)
- Monthly status updates — milestone completion, spend vs. plan, risks, decisions needed (step 2)
- Portfolio dashboard — consolidated status and budget utilization for the CEO (step 3)
Time Estimate: Initiative documentation 2 hours/initiative at onboarding; monthly status updates 30 min/initiative × ~15–25 active initiatives ≈ 90–150 hours/year; FP&A portfolio summary 2 hours/month ≈ 24 hours/year; CEO portfolio review 30 min within the monthly operating review.

steps.activity: Each strategic initiative documented in initiative tracker: (a) initiative name, strategic priority alignment, sponsor (C-Suite), lead (senior manager), (b) business case: expected outcome, financial impact, timeline, resource requirement, (c) milestones with dates, (d) status: On Track (green), At Risk (amber), Off Track (red), Complete
Monthly: initiative leads update status: (a) milestone completion, (b) budget spent vs. plan, (c) risks and issues, (d) decisions needed from C-Suite

Monthly: FP&A compiles initiative status summary for CEO: (a) portfolio dashboard: all initiatives with status, (b) budget utilization: total initiative spend vs. budget, (c) at-risk initiatives with root cause and recommended actions, (d) completed initiatives with outcome vs. business case

CEO reviews initiative portfolio with C-Suite at monthly operating review: (a) course-correct at-risk initiatives, (b) approve scope/budget changes, (c) celebrate completions, (d) archive completed initiatives
